title: Creamy Coffee Fudge
style: Soft, buttery coffee tablet-style fudge with a hit of espresso and coffee liqueur.
description: A rich, creamy coffee fudge made with condensed milk, demerara sugar, and instant espresso, spiked with coffee liqueur and set in a 20 cm square tin.
steps: Line a 20 cm square tin with baking parchment.

Stir the coffee into the milk until thoroughly mixed, then pour into a large non-stick saucepan with the remaining ingredients except the coffee liqueur. Melt everything together over a low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.

Bring to a steady boil for 10–15 minutes, stirring continuously and scraping the base of the pan to stop it catching. The mixture should reach 113–115°C on a sugar thermometer; if you don't have one, drop a little into ice-cold water — it's ready when it forms a soft ball that doesn't stick to your fingers.
Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes, then add the coffee liqueur (if using) and mix thoroughly.

Beat the mixture until it just loses its shine and becomes very thick, about 5–10 minutes. The longer you beat once it thickens, the more crumbly the fudge; for a smoother set, beat only until it comes away from the sides of the pan and is just pourable.
Press into the prepared tin with the back of a spoon and leave to set before cutting into squares.
tips: Stir constantly during the boil and scrape the base — sugar and condensed milk catch and burn quickly.
Beat for texture: stop early for smooth and dense, keep going for a firmer, crumblier tablet-style fudge.
Keeps for up to 2 weeks in an airtight container at room temperature.
Leave out the coffee liqueur for an alcohol-free version — the fudge sets just the same.
